questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.preview_text: Find speed from a supplied velocity vector.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Evaluate the two velocity components at the stated time and take their Euclidean magnitude.
provenance.year_basis: This tariff only evaluates a given two-dimensional vector and its magnitude; no vector calculus or vector constant-acceleration formula is needed.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.preview_text: Find the magnitude and direction of static incline friction.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Resolve the known normal reaction to determine the horizontal force, then balance along the incline and use the signed result to identify friction’s direction.
provenance.year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.preview_text: Find acceleration down a rough inclined plane after release.

context.shared_stem_html: Original question information and preceding context. Only the selected unit is scored:

provenance.difficulty_basis: Recalculate the normal reaction after the horizontal force is removed, model kinetic friction and apply Newton’s second law down the slope.
provenance.year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.preview_text: Derive a force-parameter relation from a motion direction.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Add the two coplanar force vectors and use proportional components of the resultant, parallel to the initial motion from rest, to establish the printed relation.
provenance.year_basis: Adding two supplied force vectors and applying Newton’s second law in fixed component directions is AS scope; no general planar kinematic formula is needed.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.preview_text: Find a fixed-direction travel distance under a resultant force.

context.shared_stem_html: Original question information and preceding context. Only the selected unit is scored:

provenance.difficulty_basis: Use the parameter relation explicitly printed in (a), determine the resultant-force magnitude and apply scalar constant-acceleration displacement from rest along the fixed straight path.
provenance.year_basis: The mark scheme explicitly allows taking the resultant-force magnitude followed by scalar s=ut+½at². The planar context does not require the additional A level vector suvat extension.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.preview_text: Explain the direction of ground friction on a supported rod.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Identify the leftward horizontal component of tension and use horizontal equilibrium to infer the opposing friction direction.
provenance.year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
